When the solution is urgent and expensive, pause and verify‼️

This was one of the most stressful veterinary experiences I’ve had.

After a long international flight, my cat began vomiting, so I brought him to this clinic. He was alert, active, and even playful at the time, which made the situation feel less immediately critical from my perspective. Despite this, after initial tests and X-rays, I was told he likely had an intestinal blockage and urgently needed surgery at another hospital, estimated at around $14,000. I was also told that waiting could be dangerous.

When we asked to review the X-rays and understand the diagnosis, the explanation did not provide enough clarity to justify such an urgent and invasive recommendation. We also asked about anti-nausea treatment, but were told it would not help.

We decided to seek a second opinion. At the other clinic, one of the first questions we were asked was what medications had already been given to help manage his vomiting. When I explained that no anti-nausea treatment had been administered, this seemed to raise some concern.

They proceeded with medical treatment without surgery, and my cat improved significantly within a short period of time.

What concerns me most is how quickly a high-cost surgical path was presented as the only option, without sufficient explanation or attempting supportive care first. The level of pressure and urgency added significant emotional distress during an already difficult moment.

I strongly encourage pet owners to carefully review recommendations and consider a second opinion before proceeding with major decisions.

Photo taken during the visit.

Reply :

Thank you for your response. I appreciate that the X-rays were reviewed and explained at the time.

However, after seeking additional opinions, three different veterinarians independently reviewed the same X-rays and identified the findings as stool rather than an obstruction. This leaves me with an honest question — how could something later recognized as stool be initially interpreted as a likely blockage requiring urgent surgery?

I fully understand the need for caution in potentially serious cases, but this difference in interpretation is what made the experience particularly stressful for me.

I had a deeply upsetting experience at Vancouver Downtown Pet Hospital with Dr. Alan Namazi.

Before posting a standard response claiming “no record found,” I want to be clear that I am a real client and my cat was seen at this clinic. I am not including identifying details here for privacy reasons, but I am willing to verify directly if the clinic genuinely wants to investigate.

During the visit, Dr. Namazi acknowledged that my cat had diabetes but described it as “early stage” and did not provide any treatment plan, monitoring guidance, or urgency around managing the condition. As a pet owner, I relied on that professional assessment.

My cat’s condition worsened and ultimately resulted in his death. I strongly believe that proper care, guidance, or follow-up could have made a difference.

Dismissing reviews like this as “false” without meaningful investigation only adds to the frustration and lack of trust.

I am sharing this so other pet owners will be cautious, ask more questions, and consider getting a second opinion when dealing with this vet.
